claims.statement: Kast admits the manifest-owned selected guidance composition and exact provider resources under its setup lock. CLI-only is the default. Explicit MCP composition adds transport preparation. Exact legacy ownership permits cleanup after success while providers own plugin configuration and cache.
Destructive recovery is restricted to an exact named tree beneath an absolute physically canonical installation directory, rejecting symlinked installation roots and paths outside that ownership.
Verified shutdown fences new work, disables the coordinator, retires requests and then the selected host, stopping on a finite stage-qualified rejection before reporting Stopped.

Force reset capability constructors are private and their effect transitions consume single-use leases: erasure requires successfully retired QuiescentReset ownership and records the erased fence before issuing its successor.
Force reinstall cold-stages through the embedded installer with --stage-only and a restricted child environment before admitting fresh payload bytes; staged bytes do not establish active readiness.
Failed staging or payload completion triggers stopped-state compensation. A failed compensation preserves both the original failure and recovery failure instead of reporting completion.

Control and Host release records, artifacts and installation inputs have independent ownership; fresh installation composes a contract-compatible pair, while Control metadata requires no Host archive.

Control-only upgrade admits the running Host before retiring Control and repeats Host admission after replacement without broker startup. Failure after retirement uses Control recovery and preserves original and recovery failures.
Exact reinstall and force reset stage Control without a Host artifact and complete through the existing fence owner without broker activation. Stage-only and control-only upgrade cannot be combined.

Native installation dispatch binds the sole HOME-derived installation; public uninstall rejects alternate or nonphysical roots before owned removal, preserving the canonical installation and Host files on rejection.

The existing installation and reset effect owners reject symlinked ancestors before directory creation or root detachment; public executable publication separately rejects aliased destination parents before writing.

Assembled-product acceptance stages production Control in an owned HOME, verifies canonical cold staging and publication, then stages the receipted Host, creates an empty canonical mutation database and invokes the real published native uninstall, requiring owned Host, Control, public executable and user-state removal while preserving an unrelated sentinel; it does not establish live IDE or Codex behavior.

The opt-in native check uses the sole normal user installation and IDEA profile, requires real compiler queries for C1/P1, C2/P1 and C2/P2, verifies unchanged host identities through Control replacement and unchanged Control through Host installation, then requires original-byte restoration with a fresh Control generation.

The native inventory rejects bounded entry and byte overflow before hashing the crossing input, while runtime installation identity derives from the physical root and ordered immutable payload bytes rather than the archive checksum.

Native restoration retains a possibly unavailable legacy original loaded-version projection but requires private production readiness, matching runtime identity and epoch, and a fresh Control generation; candidate Control status requires verified versions and an admitted live host.

Native evidence preserves each component source revision independently and permits at most three fresh semantic RUNs only for the exact typed MOVED freshness rejection at MODEL_CAPTURE or CONTENT_REVALIDATION with the declared restart_read instruction, retaining every rejection; helper tests cannot establish the live mixed-version proof.

The public installer parses the Codex plugin choice once. Component and stage-only installation skip it by default, explicit plugin installation needs a paired install, and former MCP registration flags remain aliases.

Checkout installation needs the selected IDEA executable JBR with Java 25 or newer before Gradle and scopes Java to its children. Exactly one fully quoted JAVA_VERSION declaration is necessary. Installed Control launchers select modes in one native executable without JVM setup and pass nonempty HOME and TMPDIR as system properties.

Full native uninstall retains a receipt-bound exterior retirement journal through staged cleanup and delegates locked physical user-state inventory and read-only settled mutation inspection to existing owners; unknown, live, changed or unsettled evidence remains protected.

The product CI lane retains one complete versioned candidate. Main reuses same-repository PR bytes only after successful producer admission and equality of complete source trees. Documentation-only validation needs no product candidate.

Successful main product validation promotes retained candidate bytes to the developer channel without another build. The publisher examines producer and digest provenance, admits exact retries, and preserves latest when main advances. Documentation-only validation completes without product publication.

CI pins BellSoft Liberica NIK 25.0.2+13 and configures Gradle cache transport with routine PR reads and main push/dispatch writes. Native handoff retains native metrics and finite build outcomes, produces one unified executable with -Os, and transfers its exact bytes; configured cache transport does not prove an observed cache hit.
Candidate versions use the CI run number within the installer's 32-bit semantic-version range, while the identity record retains the full run ID and producer attempt.

Host receipt admission qualifies device changes through stable root inode and owner evidence and permits missing recorded entries only for protected removal, while exact reinstall inventory remains necessary.

Default installer failure presentation reads bounded stream tails and prioritizes rejection and recovery details over routine telemetry. It keeps the child exit status and limits display to 12 details plus one truncation notice. Verbose output keeps complete child streams.
Force reset completes through InstalledReset with single-use payload and exact-fence admission, exposes no startup or readiness capability, and reports RESET_INSTALLED without a service generation.

Managed composition captures typed preimages and coordinates existing Control and Host owners under admitted locks. Pending recovery precedes selection, uses its recorded transaction, and preserves unresolved fencing. The bounded main catalog keeps original candidate provenance and main-ancestry order.

Force retirement admits native worker modes through the shared process adapter, which skips only leading consumed runtime-option families. Management and installer modes remain excluded. Bare -Dfoo, unsupported -X forms, and misplaced selectors remain application data. Unknown modes or unavailable arguments reject before erasure. PID and start identity stay necessary. The native composition case proves retirement of an MCP client with -Xmx256m and removal of disposable Control.

Mac qualification imports the assembled Control archive's executable into the existing publicLauncherTest suite before candidate sealing. The workflow initializes the existing Gradle cache owner before qualification and retains the suite's XML and HTML reports.

The local product gate qualifies clean source under validation-only version 0.0.0 and full commit/tree identity, explicitly fixes component versions, rechecks source after Gradle succeeds, and requires matching staged Control metadata before VALIDATED. Dry-run and rejection cannot claim completed qualification or inherit prior success.
Full and affected source validation and local product qualification request single-use Gradle daemons while retaining disk caches; client cleanup does not prove synchronous daemon retirement.

On graph timeout or cancellation, optional daemon diagnostics bound helper time and output, check invocation association and process start identity before and after attachment, and publish only complete confirmed output without replacing the graph failure or preventing client cleanup.

Routine membership inspection uses separate streamed product and native-input dry-run phases with a default 600-second execution deadline, bounded diagnostics and owned process-group cleanup. Both Gradle commands use two workers, a 5 GiB heap and single-use daemons. Prior success and phase reports are replaced before work; continuation requires successful execution and complete task proofs, while failures and observed cancellation reject with nonzero status.
Managed headless assembly admits pinned inputs and a new owned root, then uses the existing installer with private state. Assembly alone grants no Host readiness.
Whole-plugin exclusions reject unknown IDs, Host roots, and dependencies of kept plugins. The manifest records input digests, component decisions, and exact kept or removed files.
Selected IDEA metadata admission accepts reviewed 262 and 263 release lines while preserving canonical home and executable selection.
Host release assembly packages separate archive and descriptor variants for reviewed IDEA 262 and 263 release lines.
The installed Kast dispatcher exits without local qualification. The manual pre-push mode still starts the full product gate after the cheap checks pass.
Native container tasks belong to the management command and dispatch before installed-root admission. The checkout builder prepares source images separately from ordinary installed use.

Control staging excludes share/kast/container. The producer guard and installed-product runner reject that directory and its descendants. Separate task-VM and installation helpers remain in the Control payload.

The installed-product runner copies the actual native executable into an isolated directory and invokes container --help and container run --help without HOME, host tools on PATH, or installed resources. Both invocations must succeed and describe Colima, image selection, and workspace selection. This admission covers standalone help, not task completion or live semantic behavior.
